question: Under the official repository's explicit first-channel loader semantics, does an exact same-periodogram Gaussian surrogate reproduce higher-order Newson residual structure at unresolved radii but fail at visible radii?

primary_source.citation: Lesne, Gousseau, Ladjal and Newson, Neural Film Grain Rendering, Computer Graphics Forum 44(2), 2025

bounded_source_selection.selection_rule: Exclude every P4CH selected index. For each radius in ascending frozen order, sort eligible rows by SHA-256 of 'u6.p4ci-v1|test|index|img_name|seed|radius'; require clean and grain members; require globally unique img_name; take first 16.
bounded_source_selection.member_integrity: central/local identity, method, size, CRC32, exact member SHA-256, single-frame PNG and clean/grain geometry
bounded_source_selection.decode_contract: Accept only uint8 L or RGB single-frame PNG. Convert L directly or RGB by exact channel index 0, then drop first row and column as the official loader; crop bottom/right to a multiple of 16 only for features.

comparison.normalization: per-row residual mean subtraction and population-RMS division
comparison.gaussian_control: four deterministic real-valued random-phase surrogates per row, preserving the exact residual periodogram and zero DC
comparison.distance_ratio: Per row/family, target-to-median-Gaussian feature RMSE divided by median pairwise Gaussian-to-Gaussian feature RMSE.
comparison.radius_summary: median row ratio per family and median across the three families

branch_rule.pass: Retain a research-only official synthetic-reference radius boundary and open a separate runtime LOD experiment.
branch_rule.fail: Close this disjoint official-dataset boundary without row, channel, radius, feature, seed or gate rescue; retain P4BS Gaussian and require a materially different observable.

forbidden: download the full archive or read unselected PNG members
replace missing members, mix RGB channels or tune rows/features/gates after target reads
copy or execute academic neural code/weights or train a final-RGB model
claim real-film, stock, process, scanner, product or visual-safety evidence
claim_ceiling: Bounded noncommercial synthetic-reference evidence about higher-order sufficiency of exact-spectrum Gaussian surrogates under the official first-channel loader; not measured film, calibration, visual safety or product admission.
